title: Homage to the nine

units.pause_note: The praṇava is said apart, before the formula, as at the start of a mantra.

words.gram: compound, f. dat. pl. (written in two parts)
words.meaning: to the deities, the nine grahas beginning with Āditya

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with a bahuvrīhi inside (ādityādi, ‘beginning with Āditya’)
samasa.vigraha: आदित्य आदिर्येषां ते आदित्यादयः नव ग्रहाः, ते देवताः, ताभ्यः
samasa.meaning: to the deities that are the nine grahas, Āditya first

morphology.note: repeated: ‘homage, homage’, a common close of a salutation.

translation.literal: Om. To the deities, the nine grahas beginning with Āditya, homage, homage.
translation.readable: Om. Homage, homage to the nine grahas, with the Sun the first of them.

meaning: The salutation that closes the sūktam: after each graha has been honoured in turn, the nine are saluted together as deities, with Āditya, the Sun, named first. The words name no other deity and add nothing to the nine salutations before them; their work is to gather the recitation into one act.
in_the_rite: Step 10 (close), first formula, before the śānti.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: The witness writes the compound in two parts (आदित्यादि नवग्रहदेवताभ्यो); it is one word. The svara marks are the witness’s.
